headline: A former president of the Italian bank Fideuram was reportedly tricked by a fake WhatsApp message and an AI-copied voice into sending about 95 million euros, and at least 36 million euros are still missing.
score_reason: Lowered by 1 from 7: the scam happened in February 2026, and this is a second-hand report of another paper's story.
importance_line: What changed: the case shows that a fake message plus a copied voice can move tens of millions of euros out of a bank, which affects bank staff and customers first, then banks and prosecutors, and the doubt is that this is a press report, not a court finding, of an ongoing investigation with no outcome yet.
summary: L'Unione Sarda, citing Corriere della Sera, reports that Paolo Molesini, a former president of the Italian bank Fideuram, was tricked in February 2026 by a fake WhatsApp message that seemed to come from a senior executive of its parent bank Intesa and by a call in which scammers copied a lawyer's voice with AI tools, and about 95 million euros was sent, mostly to China and Hong Kong. A large part was recovered, but at least 36 million euros vanished into cryptocurrency and Milan prosecutors are still tracing it; the scam dates from February and was reported on 3 October.
notes: Scam dates from February 2026 (no exact day given), so a full 'FOLLOW-UP of <date>' could not be written; marked NEW because the first public report is today and the summary says the scam is months old.
